quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Can you cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another car?

options.text: Yes.
No.
Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the car ahead is driving below the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no driver can cross them, except to turn into a driveway or business entrance. You cannot pass another car over a solid yellow line.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Solid white lines cannot be crossed. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow light at an intersection mean?

options.text: Go.
Yield to other cars.
Slow down and prepare to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming next. Slow down and be ready to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, you may continue through with caution.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Two-way left turn.
Two-way traffic.
Minimum speed limit.

questions.explanation: This sign tells you the direction traffic must flow on a one-way street. You must drive in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk at the bicyclist to let them know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed up to pull in front of the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give bicyclists plenty of space. They have less protection than drivers and passing too fast can push them off course.

questions.question: When stopped by police, what documents must you show?

options.text: Proof of insurance.
Your driver's license.
Proof of registration.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must have and show your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. All three documents are required in your vehicle when driving.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign indicate?

options.text: The start of a no passing zone.
A railroad crossing is ahead.
A school zone is ahead.
Construction work ahead.

questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn of construction, maintenance, or emergency work.

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When a car to your left arrives at an unmarked intersection at the same time as you.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when entering from a garage, driveway, or alley. You must also yield to pedestrians on an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the engine.
Turn on hazard lights and hold the steering wheel firmly.
Use extra force to steer, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
Slam on the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use extra force to steer, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: If power steering fails, you will need to use more force to steer. Reduce your speed and pull off the road to a safe place to stop.

questions.question: You see a "Merging traffic" sign on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Honk at incoming traffic.
Keep your current speed.
Speed up to avoid slowing traffic.
Move to another lane, if safe, to let traffic enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane, if safe, to let traffic enter.
questions.explanation: When traffic is merging, move to another lane if it is safe. This makes room for vehicles entering the freeway.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line in the middle. What does this tell you?

options.text: Traffic flows in both directions on this road.
Traffic flows in only one direction on this road.
The road is being repaired.
You must stay to the left of the broken yellow lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic flows in both directions on this road.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass slower cars when it is safe.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel sharply to force the vehicle back on the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement slowly.
Brake hard and stop immediately.
Slow down gently with the brakes. Then turn the steering wheel to safely return to the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gently with the brakes. Then turn the steering wheel to safely return to the pavement.
questions.explanation: Keep your wheels on the shoulder and slow down by gently applying the brakes. Once you reach a safe speed, turn the steering wheel to get back on the pavement. Do not jerk the steering wheel sharply.

questions.question: A leaking exhaust system is dangerous because it can cause:

options.text: Hearing loss.
Air pollution.
Carbon monoxide poisoning.
Poor engine performance.

questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes fumes from the vehicle and keeps them out of the passenger area. A leak allows dangerous carbon monoxide gas to enter the car. Fix any leaks in the exhaust system right away.

questions.question: Points on your driving record:

options.text: Are nothing to worry about.
Are good to have on your record.
Help you get a driving job.
Should be avoided.

questions.explanation: Points are added to your driving record when you are convicted of a traffic violation. Too many points will cause you to lose your driving privilege.

questions.question: How should you handle a driver who is tailgating you?

options.text: Speed up to create more space between the cars.
Brake hard to make them back away.
Change lanes or slow down to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently for tailgating cars. If someone is following too closely, slow down or change lanes to let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: A bus is signaling to enter the main road after a stop. You must:

options.text: Honk to show that you see them.
Move to the left lane.
Yield to the bus.
Speed up to pass the bus.

questions.explanation: You must yield to any bus signaling to return to traffic after stopping. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to allow the bus to safely enter the road.

questions.question: When is it appropriate to honk your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop suddenly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to a dangerous situation.

questions.question: When you see an accident ahead, you should:

options.text: Stay focused on your own driving.
Keep driving and do not slow down.
Stop if you were involved or if help has not arrived yet.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not stop to look at an accident unless you are involved or emergency services have not arrived. Keep your focus on driving and watch for people near the road. Do not drive to accidents just to see them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A steep hill going downward.
A crossing road is ahead.
No right turns allowed.
A narrow bridge ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. They are usually yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you about a steep downhill section ahead. Adjust your speed to prevent brake damage or crashes.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Any lights work the same in fog.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: If traffic is backing up behind you because you are driving slowly, what should you do?

options.text: Drive even slower.
Pull off the right side of the road and let other cars pass.
Do not let other cars pass you.
Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and let other cars pass.
questions.explanation: Driving slower than other traffic is dangerous. On a two-lane road, if you are driving so slowly that cars are backing up behind you, you must pull over to the right and let them pass. Only drive much slower than the speed limit if road conditions require it.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with its siren and/or flashing lights approaching, you must immediately:

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle is using its lights, siren, or other warning devices, you must immediately drive to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than car drivers.
They always have the right-of-way.
They do not have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers do not see motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians even when looking. These road users are harder to spot because they are smaller, move faster, and have less visible lights. Watch carefully for these smaller and more vulnerable road users to prevent crashes.

questions.question: What should you do when preparing to turn left?

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking your rearview mirror.
Move into the left lane.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Before turning left, signal three to five seconds ahead of time. Check your rearview mirror often as you slow down gradually. On a multi-lane road, move into the left lane before you reach the intersection. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, and turn only when it is safe.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at a four-way stop sign at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver can go without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, if two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on your right has the right-of-way. You must wait and let them go first. You can then proceed when it is safe.
